defects.description: Back-view overlay is rotated ~70-90 degrees against the body. She lies face down with her head at image-left and the blanket over her hips at image-right, so the spine should run left-to-right from the base of her neck toward the blanket. The two shoulder blades sit on the head side (~0.31-0.48, 0.49-0.77) and hip side (~0.52-0.71, 0.50-0.73) of that line, i.e. along the body axis, as if her head were at the top of the frame; the hip-side blade lies on her mid back. Gross and visible at thumbnail size.

notes: The old side-view flip (vertebral bodies along the skin, spinous processes hanging into the body) is gone: the overlay is now a symmetric back view. But the whole overlay is rotated, so the spine is still misoriented for a face-down patient. Segment count (~16 along the drawn column) not graded, per instructions. About 6 small red tender points sit either side of the drawn spine (matches brief). Instrument: chrome pen-shaped adjuster with a black rubber tip and no needle, held against her upper back. Practitioner face out of frame (top edge = shirt). Patient: near (left) arm continuous to the image-left edge, far arm hidden, legs under the blanket, no feet or patient hands visible. Background console (top right) has no readable text.

The brief asked for him to stand behind her with only his two hands visible. Hand placement itself meets the brief (fingertips either side of the back of her neck just below the skull), so this is a composition deviation, not an anatomy defect.

Overlay continues from the skull base down the whole cervical and upper-thoracic spine to about mid-back (~y 0.87); the brief asked for the skull base and upper neck only. On her midline and correctly oriented.

notes: Mirrored-hand fix confirmed. The practitioner faces the camera: his right arm (image-left) runs continuously to the hand on her left neck, and his left arm (image-right) to the hand on her right neck. Both thumbs are up, consistent with reaching round from the front, and no arm feeds the wrong hand. Her own hands hang at her sides, so the patient no longer touches her jaw. Practitioner face out of frame (top edge = shirt and her hair bun); her face is in profile (allowed). Overlay: occipital base and cervical column on her midline. Red glow on the suboccipital and upper-neck muscles both sides, as briefed. Background: anatomy poster (title illegible) and a blank console screen; no readable text.

The lumbar spine (side view, spinous processes toward the table), lateral pelvis and hip-joint glow are well placed.
Back of his head touches/clips the left frame edge; brief asked for the whole body in frame (toes are in frame).

notes: Proportions re-measured (landmarks crop r2__cond-lbp-assess-a__landmarks.png). Body length vertex to heel is ~1960 px. Hip joint (~0.483,0.555) to ankle = 932 px (raised) / 936 px (resting) vs ~913 px expected (0.466 of body length). Chin-to-hip ~705 px vs ~694 expected; shoulder-to-wrist 624 px (normal). On last round's hand scale (hand 234 px = 19 cm) the leg is ~76 cm (was ~64 cm). Legs are clearly longer than the torso, and the body reads normal at thumbnail size. The hand is ~12% large relative to body length (not flagged). Feet: raised left foot (medial view, big toe uppermost) and resting right foot are both natural with 5 toes, each on the correct leg. Practitioner face out of frame (open collar only). His right hand steadies the hip and his left presses just above the raised ankle, as briefed. Red glow sits on the two lowest lumbar segments and the hip joint. Background consoles show no readable text; a teal highlight on the exercise ball belongs to the ball, not the overlay.
